quick_facts.label: Where the role comes from
quick_facts.value: India's Digital Personal Data Protection Act, 2023 defines a Data Protection Officer as an individual appointed by a Significant Data Fiduciary under section 10 of the Act.

quick_facts.label: Who must appoint one
quick_facts.value: Under section 10(2)(a) of the Act, a Significant Data Fiduciary shall appoint a Data Protection Officer.

quick_facts.label: Based in India, answers to the board
quick_facts.value: The Act says the Data Protection Officer shall be based in India and be an individual responsible to the Board of Directors or similar governing body of the Significant Data Fiduciary.

sections.heading: What a data protection officer does
paragraphs: The Digital Personal Data Protection Act, 2023 gives the Data Protection Officer of a Significant Data Fiduciary two named duties: to represent the Significant Data Fiduciary under the provisions of the Act, and to be the point of contact for its grievance redressal mechanism.
This guide covers only what the Act itself says about the role. Companies usually give the officer wider privacy work, which varies from company to company and is not described here.
bullets: Represent the company (the Significant Data Fiduciary) under the Act.
Be the point of contact for the company's grievance redressal mechanism.

sections.heading: Where the role sits
paragraphs: The Act requires the Data Protection Officer to be based in India and to be responsible to the Board of Directors or a similar governing body of the Significant Data Fiduciary.
bullets: Common routes into this job on the Career Tree map: Compliance Executive.
Less common routes on the map: Corporate Counsel; Information Security Analyst.
